items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: Dad was lucky that he could get people to play instrumentations... Bob loved him enough and knew what he could do that he would give him license to be able to write pretty much whatever he wants

ctx.x: So I’m struggling to ask my question, but does music have to have a deeper meaning other than it’s just beautiful music?

I think it does not. I think it can just be beautiful. If you read the liner notes on that album you see when he said, “Why did you name that ‘Sound—.’” He said, “It’s a piece that sounds.” That’s what Dad quoted, and I think that’s what he was thinking just beautiful sound and stuff. We would — this is really interesting — but we would get together sometimes and he and I would cry just about beautiful sounds that we would hear and beautiful pieces that we would hear, and that kind of stuff. So beauty to him…
do that he would give him license to be able to write pretty much whatever he wants to, which is a really neat thing.
